problem: REVERIE gives only short, high-level instructions (e.g., 'Empty the washing machine on level one'). Prior VLN agents such as DUET, HAMT and HOP were designed for fine-grained step-by-step instructions and perform poorly when they have to infer a navigation plan themselves. Existing LLM-as-planner work (SayCan, Huang et al., Inner Monologue, LLM-Planner) plans atomic manipulation actions in small, simple scenes and has not been applied to large multi-room, multi-floor REVERIE buildings.
motivation: High-level commands are closer to what people actually say to domestic robots, but they lack the route detail VLN agents depend on. LLMs hold commonsense knowledge about where objects are and how to move through houses, so they could turn a concise command into fine-grained steps. To do this in large, complex environments the LLM must be environment-aware and re-plan from what the agent currently sees.
key_idea: The agent 'chats' with an LLM during navigation. At the start the LLM names the target object and its likely room; each time a CLIP-based perceiver detects a room change, the LLM is prompted with the current room and visible objects to write the next step-by-step instruction. All of this is concatenated with the original instruction and fed to a DUET-style navigator.
insight: Adding LLM-generated text (goal object + likely room + scene-conditioned step instructions) to the input of a trained graph navigator improves both navigation and grounding, even with a small GPT-2, and the pieces are complementary. In Table 2 (val-unseen), GOSP alone gives the larger grounding gain (RGSPL 26.82→28.24) and SODP alone the larger navigation gain (SPL 40.49→42.94); both together reach SPL 43.60 / RGSPL 28.72. The authors attribute SODP's lower grounding to step text diluting the target object mention. Conditioning the step planner on the ROASP scene description beats a fixed static prompt (Table 3: SPL 41.74 → 42.94). In a 100-task human study, retrieving the closest FGR2R demonstration via Sentence-BERT matters most: removing it drops Relevancy from 2.06 to 1.41, versus 1.64 when ROASP is removed. The reproduced HLI baseline (SR 52.71) is below HM3D-DUET's published 55.89, so part of the 'large margin' in the ablation reflects the weaker reproduced baseline.
method: Base navigator: HM3D-DUET (dual-scale graph transformer, same pretrained model and HM3D-AutoVLN augmented data), fine-tuned on REVERIE; chooses among nav-graph nodes and grounds the target object.

Goal-Oriented Static Planning (GOSP): run once at the start with frozen GPT-2 and in-context prompts. It first completes 'Task: <instr> Goal: The target object is:' to extract the object, then answers 'Where does a <obj> can usually appear in a house?' using one fixed demo (microwave→kitchen). Output format: 'Goal: The target object is X. It is usually in Y.'

Room-and-Object Aware Scene Perceiver (ROASP): zero-shot CLIP scores each panoramic view against 'a photo of a {c}' prompts. Room codebook comes from MP3D semantic labels, object codebook from REVERIE train. Room scores are averaged over views and the argmax is taken; the top-3 objects are kept.

Scene-Oriented Dynamic Planning (SODP): GPT-2 prompt = 'At this step, I am in <room>, I can see <objs>' + one step-by-step demonstration + the task and previous steps. It generates the next fine-grained step (e.g., 'Step 1: Exit the bedroom').

Dynamic Demonstration Selection: the REVERIE instruction and all FGR2R-train low-level R2R instructions are embedded with Sentence-BERT. The step-decomposed instruction of the highest-cosine match becomes the SODP demonstration.

Interactive prompting / instruction update: the assembled instruction W=[HLI, GOSP, SODP] is WordPiece-tokenized as the navigator's text input. SODP is re-triggered whenever the ROASP room prediction changes between timesteps, and the new step is appended. The original high-level instruction is kept to add tolerance to planning noise.

setting.backbone: HM3D-DUET graph transformer navigator (fine-tuned) + GPT-2 (frozen, in-context planner) + CLIP (frozen, scene perceiver) + Sentence-BERT (demo retrieval)
setting.training_data: REVERIE train split, starting from the HM3D-DUET pretrained model and the same HM3D-AutoVLN augmented data. Fine-tuned 30,000 iterations, batch size 4, lr 1e-5, on one RTX 3090. The FGR2R train set is used only as an in-context demonstration pool.
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (per-view image + orientation features) + object features from REVERIE-provided bounding boxes; CLIP room/object labels converted to text
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (DUET-style node selection) + selecting the target object among candidate boxes
setting.privileged: standard REVERIE object bounding-box annotations used for object features/grounding candidates (benchmark default); otherwise none

numbers.extra: HM3D-AutoVLN pretraining/augmented data (same as HM3D-DUET); FGR2R train used as demonstration pool

numbers_note: Only val-unseen and test-unseen are reported; there are no val-seen results. Ablations (Tables 2-3) are on REVERIE val-unseen and include HLI+GOSP (OSR 59.92 / SR 55.28 / SPL 42.46 / RGS 37.13 / RGSPL 28.24), HLI+SODP (60.72 / 56.26 / 42.94 / 36.80 / 27.81) and Static planning (60.24 / 55.35 / 41.74 / 36.30 / 27.03). The ablation 'HLI (Baseline)' is a reproduced HM3D-DUET (SR 52.71 / SPL 40.49), lower than the published HM3D-DUET row in Table 1 (SR 55.89 / SPL 40.85). Some deltas quoted in the ablation text do not match the table: the RGSPL gap between SODP and GOSP is 0.43, while the text says 1.43.
results: MiC sets a new REVERIE state of the art at publication. On test-unseen it reaches SPL 41.97 and RGSPL 26.17, versus 38.88 / 22.68 for the strongest baseline HM3D-DUET (+3.09 SPL, +3.49 RGSPL); SR rises only modestly (55.74 vs 55.17). On val-unseen it reaches SR 56.97 / SPL 43.60 / RGSPL 28.72, versus 55.89 / 40.85 / 26.76 for HM3D-DUET. Ablations show GOSP and SODP are complementary, and scene-aware dynamic planning beats static planning.
limitations: Uses a weak LLM (GPT-2): human ratings of generated plans are only 2.06/3 relevancy and 1.93/3 rationality, and step-by-step plan text can add noise that hurts object grounding (the SODP-only variant has lower RGSPL than GOSP-only).

Evaluated only on REVERIE; there is no analysis of LLM choice or size, and SR gains over HM3D-DUET are small (test SR +0.57). Part of the ablation gain comes from a reproduced baseline weaker than the published HM3D-DUET.

Re-planning depends on zero-shot CLIP room classification with a fixed MP3D room codebook and REVERIE object vocabulary, so misclassified rooms can trigger spurious or missed re-plans. The LLM output only enters as extra text to a navigator that must still be fine-tuned.
